messages:
Alicia: Quick sync — we need a canonical, unambiguous set of metric defs for the apples->apples run next Tue. People are using TTFT/TPOT/goodput differently across harnesses.

Sam H: +1. Can we start with short, formal defs and then add measurement guidance? I can update the README if we agree. :thumbsup:

Dinesh: My high-level take: TTFT should include the full scheduling/queueing delay that a real request sees. Otherwise we understate user latency. TPOT should reflect useful work (tokens/sec) not raw GPU cycles.

Mei: Proposed formal definitions (draft):
```
TTFT = t_first_token_emitted - t_request_received_at_frontend
TPOT = total_tokens_emitted_in_window / measurement_window_seconds
QPS = requests_received / measurement_window_seconds
Goodput = total_successful_tokens_emitted / effective_serving_seconds

Notes:
- p95/p99 for TTFT/latency computed over the steady-state window after warmup
- TPOT measured at steady-state and reported both as aggregate and per-model/route
```

Karthik: Clarify "effective_serving_seconds"? is that wall time or exclude scheduler idle?

Mei: Good question. I propose: effective_serving_seconds = measurement_window_seconds - scheduler_idle_seconds where scheduler_idle_seconds are periods where no batches were dispatched because of upstream throttling. We want goodput to capture actual model throughput when the runtime is actively producing tokens.

Alicia: That matches what product expects. We also need guidance on whether kernel selection/kernels switching should be allowed mid-run for apples->apples. That can change p95 a lot.

Dinesh: For apples->apples we must fix kernel and quantization profile per experiment. Kernel selection should be part of the experiment metadata, not dynamic. Otherwise you compare different runtime behaviors.

Sam H: Agreed. Also: batching heuristics matter. We should capture batch size distribution: mean, median, p90, histogram. Two runs with same QPS but different batching can have very different TPOT/TTFT profiles.

Mei: Measurement recipe I propose:
1) Warmup phase (configurable, default 60s) with cache warming toggles (kv_cache=true/false)
2) Steady-state window (default 300s) where metrics are collected
3) Tear-down window (30s) to capture tails if needed

Include flags: --kv-warm=[true|false], --kernel=explicit_name, --batch-policy=policy_name

perf-bot: nightly/regression summary posted: https://ci.redwood/example/1765432 — contains perf traces for last runs and a kcache hit-rate heatmap. :eyes:

Karthik: On KV cache behavior: report cache_hit_rate, avg_cache_lookup_latency, and separate TTFT for cold vs warmed requests. For replay harnesses we should run both cold-start traces and warmed traces.

Sam H: For replay vs synthetic: replay gives realistic seq-len and prompt distribution; synthetic lets us stress corner cases (max-length, tiny prompts). Both are needed. In the paper/run output include a small table: Replay vs Synthetic differences (seq-len distrib, batch fill, cache hits).

Alicia: We also need to avoid measuring queued requests that get dropped/retried — define a measurement policy: count only terminally successful responses for TPOT, but surface retries as a separate metric (retry_rate).

Mei: Example commands for the harness to make runs reproducible:
```bash
replay_harness \
  --trace=traces/my_replay.json \
  --metrics=ttft,tpot,kv_hit_rate,batch_stats \
  --warmup=60 --steady=300 --kv-warm=true \
  --kernel=triton_v2_q4f16 --batch-policy=continuous
```

Dinesh: For TTFT vs TPOT reporting, include both absolute numbers and normalized per-cost unit (tokens/sec per GPU). That helps cost-performance decisions.

Sam H: Regression detection rules:
- If p95(TTFT) increases by >15% and TPOT drops >10% for same trace+kernel, auto-open a regression issue.
- Use paired runs (same seed, same trace) and require 3 runs to avoid noise.

Karthik: One more operational detail: instrument kernel-selection logs so we can correlate tail events with kernel switches. Add a label `kernel_decision_reason` to traces.

Alicia: This is great. Sam — can you consolidate into a short fixture and add to infra/docs? I'll circulate to eng-sre and perf teams.

Sam H: Yup, I'll draft the README and a config template today. Will post PR with examples.

perf-bot: FYI artifact uploaded: s3://redwood-perf/1765432100/summary.html

Alicia: Thanks all. If anyone has a counter-proposal for the TTFT/TPOT formula, speak now or file an issue. :rocket:
